articles.title: Who is Shivon Zilis? Meet the Elon Musk exec who said their relationship suddenly ended
articles.summary: Neuralink director Shivon Zilis is the mother of four of Elon Musk's children and an ex-OpenAI board member. Learn more about the Canadian-born VC.
articles.body:
AI investor and developer Shivon Zilis is a longtime executive at Elon Musk's companies.

She said on X that her relationship with Musk went "from in love to let go."

A director at Neuralink, Zilis is a plaintiff in the trial and has four children with Musk.

Shivon Zilis — a longtime executive at Elon Musk's companies and the mother of four of his children — said her relationship with the billionaire ended "in a week with no warning."

In a post on X, Zilis shared a rare glimpse into Musk's romantic life.

"I feel happy that I got to show Elon how it feels to be deeply understood, nurtured, and peacefully loved with stability and gentleness," she wrote on Friday. "My heart is full knowing I got to do that, and I hope it leaves a lasting good effect."

Zilis and her employer, the Musk-owned Neuralink , didn't respond to a request for comment from Business Insider. Musk also didn't respond.

She joined Musk at OpenAI in 2016, a year after its founding, and helped helm the company during Musk's investment and his rancorous 2018 split with CEO Sam Altman.

From there, Zilis followed Musk to Tesla and his rival project, xAI.

She's now the director of operations and special projects at another of the billionaire's companies — Neuralink , a startup that makes computer chips designed to be implanted in the brain.

Zilis is also the mother to four of Musk's children.

Elon Musk's biographer, Walter Isaacson, shared a glimpse into Musk's relationship with Zilis in September 2023.

In an excerpt from Isaacson's biography of the Tesla CEO and in a post on social media, he shared a photo of Musk and Zilis with their twins — who were 16 months old at the time — sitting on each of their laps.

The biographer said the photo was taken when Musk ushered him to Zilis' house in Austin to talk about the threat AI posed to civilization.

"We were sitting on a suburban patio by a tranquil backyard swimming pool on a sunny spring day, with two bright-eyed twins learning to toddle, as Musk somberly speculated about the window of opportunity for building a sustainable human colony on Mars before an AI apocalypse destroyed earthly civilization," Isaacson said of the scene.

Here is more you need to know about Zilis:

Zilis grew up in Ontario, Canada, and is a lifelong athlete

Zilis was born in Markham, Ontario, and grew up playing ice hockey. She attended Yale University, where she played goalie on the women's ice hockey team. She graduated in 2008 with a degree in economics and philosophy.

Photos from Zilis' social media accounts, which were taken down in 2022, show Zilis surfing, zip-lining, and ice climbing.

She started her career in finance and venture capital

After graduating from Yale, Zilis got a job at IBM, where she spent three years focused on financial technologies.

She later joined early-stage venture capital fund Bloomberg Beta, where she led investment efforts in data and machine learning. Her work at Bloomberg Beta earned her a spot on Forbes' 30 Under 30 list in the venture-capital category in 2015.

Zilis worked as a project director at Tesla from 2017 to 2019, contributing her AI expertise to the Autopilot and chip design teams.

She's passionate about artificial intelligence

Zilis developed an interest in artificial intelligence around the age of 12 or 13, when she learned about the concept from the Our Lady Peace album "Spiritual Machines." It led her to read a Ray Kurzweil book by a similar name and sparked her passion for AI, she said during a 2021 address at the Canadian Undergraduate Conference on AI .

"I've basically spent pretty much all of the last decade focused in and around AI unfolding in the world in the best way possible," she said.

It was AI that led her to Musk: In 2016, Zilis joined OpenAI, a nonprofit co-founded by a group that included Musk and former Y Combinator president Sam Altman. OpenAI's stated mission is to find ways for AI to benefit humanity as a whole. The company made headlines when it released a new version of its AI chatbot, ChatGPT in 2023 .

Zilis and Musk share a love for fantasy and gaming

Like Musk, Zilis appears to have a passion for fantasy and games in the genre.

The Neuralink executive posted on X in May that "the fact that a visually rich and dynamic world can live and come alive on a laptop is insane."

"We're so normalized to the magic of gaming," Zilis said in the post. "But, when you step back and think about it, it's absolutely wild."

She also posted a photo on X in July of talismans from Elden Ring, a fantasy video game set in a world of dungeons and warriors, known for its challenging gameplay. The game is written by "A Song of Fire and Ice" author George RR Martin and produced by FromSoftware, the creators of Dark Souls. The talismans in the game have various powers, such as increasing bow range or stamina recovery.

Zilis followed up with a response to the post and said the items were "not religious or witchcraft items." She also added that they have "resonance" for her in the game, "but also to keep in mind as priorities for real life (whether literally or through analogy)."

Musk also enjoys playing Elden Ring — to the point where he's reportedly stayed up till 5:30 a.m. playing it.

In 2017, Zilis joined Neuralink, the futuristic brain microchip company also cofounded by Musk. Neuralink has a short-term goal of using implantable devices to solve brain and spine problems, and a long-term mission of achieving "symbiosis" between artificial intelligence and the human brain, according to Musk .

In her presentation at the Canadian Undergraduate Conference on AI in 2021, Zilis called Neuralink the most "complicated but also fascinating thing I've ever encountered in my life."

"AI's going to be one of the fundamentally transformative technologies humanity creates, if not the most," she said. "And so we just need to make sure, from a humanity perspective, this goes well."

In January, Noland Arbaugh became the first human patient to receive a Neuralink brain implant.

In 2020, Musk publicly sparred with the state of California over its COVID-19 lockdown restrictions, calling them "fascist" and "forcible imprisoning." He pledged that Tesla's headquarters would relocate to Texas as a result, prompting California State Assembly member Lorena Gonzalez Fletcher to tweet, "F*ck Elon Musk."

Zilis responded on Twitter, writing that Gonzalez Fletcher's tweet made her sad.

"No one's perfect but I've never met anyone who goes through more personal pain to fight for an inspiring future for humanity - and has done so tirelessly for decades," Zilis wrote. "Everyone's entitled to their opinion but mine is that there's no one I respect and admire more."

This year, she testified at Musk's civil trial against OpenAI's Sam Altman.

The trial centered on Musk's claims that Altman took his $38 million early investment in the company behind ChatGPT, then reneged on his promise that it would remain solely nonprofit.

Zillis, who joined Musk as a plaintiff in the $134 billion lawsuit that led to the trial, was a key witness , having had a front-row seat to many of the events before the six-member jury.

Zilis had twins with Musk in 2021 and bought a house in Austin

Business Insider was the first to report that Zilis had twins with the Tesla CEO , who were born in 2021. In 2022, Zilis and Musk filed a petition to change the twins' names in order to "have their father's last name and contain their mother's last name as part of their middle name," according to court documents obtained by Business Insider.

Zilis purchased a home in a gated community in Austin in August 2021.

Tesla's Gigafactory is located near Austin, and court documents obtained by Business Insider list Musk and Zilis as residents of that address. Musk, however, has said that his primary residence is a $50,000 Tesla tiny house in Boca Chica, near the SpaceX launch facility in South Texas.

She is one of several women who have children with Musk

There are eight other known living children of Musk aside from those fathered with Zilis: Five are with Musk's first wife , Justine Wilson, and three are with Musk's former girlfriend, the musician Grimes. The billionaire has said in the past that he's doing his best to help the " underpopulation crisis ."

Zilis and Musk's twins were born a few weeks before Musk and Grimes had their second child via surrogate. Musk and Grimes later had a third child in June 2022, according to a 2023 biography of Musk.

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada neste sábado (3) é a última antes do 1º turno, neste domingo, e foi encomendada pela TV Liberal. O candidato Dr Daniel (Podemos) lidera as intenções de voto, a partir dos votos válidos.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada neste sábado (3) é a última antes do 1º turno, neste domingo, e foi encomendada pela TV Liberal.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada neste sábado (3), véspera do 1º turno, mostra como está a disputa pelo governo do Pará. O candidato Dr Daniel ( Podemos ) lidera as intenções de voto, a partir dos votos válidos.

Dr Daniel à esq.; e Hana Ghassan, à dir. — Foto: Reprodução

É a forma como o TSE divulga o resultado oficial das eleições. São os votos dados nos candidatos. Esse cálculo deixa de fora os votos em branco e os votos nulos. Para vencer no 1º turno, um candidato precisa de 50% dos votos válidos mais um voto.

A Quaest leva em consideração as intenções de voto da pesquisa e o perfil de comparecimento para estimar os votos válidos . É o modelo likely voter, que considera eleitores com maior propensão a votar.

O levantamento foi encomendado pela TV Liberal e ouviu 1.800 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais, entre os dias 2 e 3 de outubro. A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número TSE: PA-04580/2026.

Veja agora o resultado com os votos totais, incluindo votos em branco, nulos e eleitores indecisos.

Dr Daniel (Podemos): 44% (eram 41% em 26 de setembro )

Veja agora a pesquisa espontânea, em que os eleitores respondem sem ter acesso a uma lista de candidatos.

Esses resultados ajudam a medir o grau de consolidação do voto. Quanto maior o número de indecisos na véspera, menos consolidado está o voto e maior a possibilidade de mudanças em relação ao resultado de domingo.

Dr Daniel (Podemos): 29% (eram 23% em 26 de setembro)

Indecisos: 45% (eram 54% em 26 de setembro)

Entre os eleitores que declaram voto em um candidato,83% dizem que a decisão é definitiva. Outros 16% afirmam que ainda podem mudar de ideia.

Muito interessado: 42% (eram 31% em 26 de setembro)

A Quaest simulou também um cenário de 2º turno. Veja os números:

Dr Daniel (Podemos): 48% (eram 47% em 26 de setembro)

Hana Ghassan (MDB): 37% (eram 36% em agosto)

articles.title: Chefe da polícia de Paris diz que protesto está fora de controle | G1
articles.standfirst: Protestos estudantis se espalham pela França em meio a confrontos com a polícia, enquanto sindicatos convocam greve e autoridades alertam para novos episódios de violência.
articles.summary: Protestos estudantis se espalham pela França em meio a confrontos com a polícia, enquanto sindicatos convocam greve e autoridades alertam para novos episódios de violência.
articles.body:
Alunos da França fazem protestos com foto em Saint-Denis, próximo a Paris. — Foto: Abdul Saboor/Reuters

O protesto estudantil que se espalhou pela França está agora "fora de controle", afirmou o chefe da polícia de Paris neste sábado (03). Ele pediu que os manifestantes retomassem ações pacíficas e alertou que as autoridades responderiam com firmeza a atos de violência e vandalismo.

A polícia de choque entrou em confronto com estudantes do ensino médio em várias regiões do país na sexta-feira (02).

Sindicatos também convocaram professores para uma greve, enquanto o governo do presidente Emmanuel Macron tentava conter os protestos, que se tornaram cada vez mais violentos .

Os estudantes reclamam das condições nas salas de aula e da falta de investimentos na educação. ( entenda os motivos dos protestos ).

Desde segunda-feira (28), cerca de 5 mil pessoas, a maioria adolescentes , foram presas em todo o país, e dezenas ficaram feridas.

Agathe Foucault, porta-voz da polícia nacional, afirmou à rádio RTL neste sábado (03) que mais de 600 policiais também ficaram feridos.

Professores e outros cidadãos foram atacados, enquanto os prejuízos materiais são estimados em dezenas de milhões de euros .

Em uma carta aberta publicada no X antes dos novos protestos previstos para a próxima terça-feira (06), o chefe da polícia de Paris , Patrice Faure, afirmou que aqueles que deram início ao movimento já não tinham controle sobre ele.

Ele pediu aos estudantes que abandonassem os bloqueios nas escolas e os atos de violência e adotassem formas pacíficas de manifestação.

"É hora de voltar a formas pacíficas de ação", escreveu Faure. Ele também afirmou que os pais têm a responsabilidade de afastar os filhos do que classificou como a influência de "manifestantes profissionais" e de seus apoiadores.

Os sindicatos estudantis convocaram uma mobilização nacional para terça-feira (06). Autoridades de segurança temem que um ato organizado no centro de Paris , em particular, provoque novos episódios de violência.

Há também preocupação de que grupos anarquistas de extrema esquerda se apropriem do movimento.

Os estudantes que bloqueiam as escolas de ensino médio protestam contra a superlotação das salas de aula, a falta frequente de professores e as condições precárias das instalações. Eles atribuem os problemas a anos de falta de investimentos na educação.

articles.title: Referência da música de concerto no Brasil, maestro Roberto Tibiriçá morre aos 72 anos em São Paulo | G1
articles.standfirst: Regente esteve à frente de algumas das principais orquestras do país e teve carreira marcada pela formação de músicos. Velório será aberto ao público no Theatro Municipal de São Paulo.
articles.summary: Regente esteve à frente de algumas das principais orquestras do país e teve carreira marcada pela formação de músicos. Velório será aberto ao público no Theatro Municipal de São Paulo.
articles.body:
O maestro Roberto Tibiriçá, um dos principais nomes da música de concerto brasileira, morreu na madrugada deste sábado (3), aos 72 anos, em São Paulo . A informação foi confirmada pelo Theatro Municipal de São Paulo e pelo Centro Cultural Teatro Guaíra, no Paraná. A causa da morte não foi divulgada.

Paulistano, Tibiriçá construiu uma carreira de mais de quatro décadas à frente de algumas das mais importantes orquestras do país, tornando-se referência na regência e na formação de novas gerações de músicos. Desde 2022, era regente titular e diretor musical da Orquestra Sinfônica do Paraná (OSP).

Em nota, o Theatro Municipal de São Paulo lamentou a morte do maestro e destacou sua importância para a música brasileira.

"Um dos nomes fundamentais da música de concerto no Brasil", afirmou a instituição, ressaltando que Tibiriçá esteve à frente da Orquestra Sinfônica Municipal em diversas ocasiões e deixou um legado marcado pela excelência artística, pela dedicação à formação musical e pela atuação nas principais orquestras do país.

Maestro Roberto Tibiriçá durante apresentação no Paraná em 2024 — Foto: Divulgação/Maringas Maciel

A carreira do maestro começou cedo. Ele iniciou sua relação com a música aos 8 anos de idade, por meio do piano, e estudou com professores como Dinorah de Carvalho, Antonio Bezzan e Gilberto Tinetti.

Ao longo da trajetória, passou por instituições como a Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira, Petrobras Sinfônica, Orquestra Sinfônica de Minas Gerais, Osesp e Orquestra Sinfônica do Paraná, entre outras.

Outro capítulo importante de sua carreira foi no Instituto Baccarelli. Em 2005, assumiu a direção artística da entidade e comandou um período de expansão e consolidação do projeto musical de Heliópolis. À frente da Orquestra Sinfônica Heliópolis, participou de apresentações marcantes e contribuiu para a formação artística de centenas de jovens músicos.

Em publicação nas redes sociais, o diretor-presidente do Centro Cultural Teatro Guaíra, Cleverson Cavalheiro, afirmou que "a música brasileira está de luto" e destacou a contribuição de Tibiriçá para o desenvolvimento artístico da Orquestra Sinfônica do Paraná.

"Perdemos um grande maestro, mas seu legado permanecerá vivo em cada músico, em cada concerto e em cada pessoa que foi tocada por sua música", escreveu.

Segundo o Teatro Guaíra, mesmo enfrentando uma doença que fragilizou sua saúde, o maestro manteve até os últimos meses o compromisso com a atividade artística. Sua última apresentação ocorreu em 16 de julho, em Londrina, à frente da OSP, no projeto Guaíra para Todos.

Entre os momentos recentes mais marcantes de sua passagem pela orquestra paranaense está a condução da Sinfonia nº 2, "Ressurreição", de Gustav Mahler, durante as comemorações dos 40 anos da OSP, em 2025. O concerto reuniu mais de 200 músicos e coralistas no palco do Guairão.

Fachada do Theatro Municipal de São Paulo, no Centro da capital paulista. — Foto: Richard Lourenço/Rede Câmara

O velório de Roberto Tibiriçá será realizado no Theatro Municipal de São Paulo e terá acesso aberto ao público.

Neste sábado (3), a cerimônia ocorrerá das 18h às 22h, no Salão Nobre do teatro. No domingo (4), a despedida continuará das 8h às 12h, no palco da Sala de Espetáculos.

O sepultamento está previsto para as 13h de domingo, no Cemitério São Paulo.

Em nota, o Theatro Municipal afirmou se solidarizar com familiares, amigos, músicos, alunos e todos aqueles que fizeram parte da trajetória do maestro.

"Seu legado permanece na música brasileira, nas orquestras que regeu e, sobretudo, nas gerações de músicos que tiveram suas trajetórias marcadas por seu trabalho e dedicação à formação musical", disse a instituição.

articles.title: Com bolo gigante, Mercado Público de Porto Alegre celebra 157 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Receita preparada por confeiteira rendeu 1.157 fatias. Ponto turístico da capital gaúcha já resistiu a incêndio e enchentes históricas, como a de 2024.
articles.summary: Programação especial neste sábado (3) reuniu tratbalhadores e visitantes. Receita foi feita com 20 quilos de doce de leite
articles.body:
O Mercado Público de Porto Alegre completa 157 anos de história neste sábado (3). Para celebrar a data, teve música e o tradicional bolo de aniversário , preparado pela confeiteira Nina Oliveira.

A receita levou 30 quilos de açúcar, 20 quilos de farinha, 288 ovos, 20 quilos de doce de leite e ganache, além de 26 litros de chantilly .

Ao meio-dia, o público se reuniu para cantar "Parabéns a Você". Foram distribuídas 1.157 fatias de torta entre os visitantes e os trabalhadores do local .

"O Mercado Público é a alma da cidade, espaço de cultura, geração de renda e símbolo da nossa resiliência. Enfrentou enchentes e incêndio ao longo da história e chega aos 157 anos ainda mais forte" disse o prefeito Sebastião Melo.

Mercado Público de Porto Alegre celebra 157 anos com bolo de mil fatias — Foto: Pedro Piegas/PMPA

Chamado de "coração da capital" pelos mercadeiros, os trabalhadores do local, o Mercado Público é um dos pontos mais movimentados da cidade e recebe milhares de visitantes todos os dias.

O ponto turístico também já enfrentou tragédias como enchentes e incêndio. Em 1941, as águas do Guaíba alcançaram 4,76 metros e invadiram o Mercado Público. Era a maior cheia registrada na cidade. Até que, em 2024, essa marca foi superada, com a água atingindo a cota de 5,37 metros . Por dias, o Centro Histórico ficou inundado.

Em 2013, o Mercado Público teve um incêndio , que destruiu parte do telhado e comprometeu estruturas, que tiveram de ser refeitas.

articles.title: França vai suspender carteira de quem usar celular ao volante | G1
articles.standfirst: A suspensão temporária da carteira de motorista para quem for flagrado usando o celular ao volante, já adotada em vários departamentos da França, passará a valer em todo o território nacional, anunciou a ministra delegada responsável pela Cidadania, Marie-Pierre Vedrenne.
articles.summary: Medida, já adotada em vários departamentos, será ampliada para todo o território nacional, anunciou a ministra Marie-Pierre Vedrenne.
articles.body:
A suspensão temporária da carteira de motorista para quem for flagrado usando o celular ao volante vai passar a valer em toda a França. — Foto: AFP (via RFI)

“Queremos mostrar que o uso do celular ao volante, por si só, já constitui um comportamento suficientemente perigoso. O alvo são justamente os motoristas comuns”, afirmou a ministra Marie-Pierre Vedrenne em entrevista publicada nesta sexta-feira (2) no jornal Le Figaro.

“É possível causar um acidente de um dia para o outro e carregar a responsabilidade por uma morte simplesmente por enviar uma mensagem”, lembrou Vedrenne. Em 2025, 3.515 pessoas morreram nas estradas francesas.

Até agora, cerca de 20 prefeituras já haviam decidido adotar a medida , segundo a ministra, entre elas as dos departamentos de Landes e Pas-de-Calais. “O uso do celular não é menos perigoso em um território do que em outro. Para que uma regra seja aceita, ela deve ser clara, compreensível e aplicada em todo o país”, justificou.

Riscos O uso do celular ao volante já é punido na França com multa de € 135 (o equivalente a cerca de R$ 864) e perda de três pontos na carteira . Com a nova medida, os motoristas também poderão ter a habilitação suspensa por um período de 15 dias a seis meses.

“A duração da suspensão será avaliada pelas autoridades de acordo com as circunstâncias e o histórico do condutor. Nos departamentos que já aplicam a medida, o período costuma ser de 15 dias . Mas também pode ser de um mês e, em alguns casos , chegar a seis meses”, acrescentou a ministra.

“É necessária uma punição real, mas proporcional”, afirmou. Segundo ela, “a suspensão será decidida e notificada pelo Secretário de Segurança Pública, e o motorista poderá apresentar suas observações no âmbito do procedimento administrativo de contestação”.

Segundo o site da Segurança Rodoviária da França, “o uso do celular ao volante triplica o risco de acidente”. Mais grave ainda, “ler uma mensagem enquanto dirige multiplica esse risco por 23, pois obriga o motorista a desviar os olhos da estrada por pelo menos cinco segundos”.

Pesquisa Quaest divulgada neste sábado (3), véspera do 1º turno, mostra como está a disputa pelo governo de São Paulo. Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) aparece com 60% dos votos válidos e Fernando Haddad, com 36%. Considerando este resultado, o governador tem chances de vencer a eleição já no primeiro turno.

É a forma como o TSE divulga o resultado oficial das eleições. São os votos dados nos candidatos. Esse cálculo deixa de fora os votos em branco e os votos nulos. Para vencer no 1º turno, um candidato precisa de 50% dos votos válidos mais um voto.

A Quaest leva em consideração as intenções de voto da pesquisa e o perfil de comparecimento para estimar os votos válidos. É o modelo likely voter, que considera eleitores com maior propensão a votar.

O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e ouviu 3.702 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais, entre os dias 2 e 3 de outubro. A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número SP-04726/2026.

articles.title: Portugal investiga uso de base militar pelos EUA em conflito com Irã | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação vai apurar se autorização dada pelo governo português aos voos americanos respeitou o direito internacional.
articles.summary: Investigação vai apurar se autorização dada pelo governo português aos voos americanos respeitou o direito internacional.
articles.body:
Presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, durante pronunciamento na Casa Branca em 18 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Evan Vucci/ Reuters

O Ministério Público de Portugal abriu uma investigação para apurar se o governo agiu dentro da lei ao autorizar o uso da Base das Lajes, nos Açores, pelos Estados Unidos durante o conflito com o Irã . O inquérito foi aberto após uma denúncia do Bloco de Esquerda, partido de oposição.

Um acordo de longa data permite que os Estados Unidos utilizem a base sem autorização prévia de Portugal em tempos de paz. Quando há um conflito, porém, o uso precisa ser aprovado pelo governo português.

Ao contrário da vizinha Espanha, Portugal autorizou a passagem de vários voos dos Estados Unidos pela Base Aérea das Lajes. A decisão provocou críticas de partidos de esquerda da oposição e abriu um debate sobre o papel do país nas operações relacionadas ao conflito com o Irã.

Em comunicado, a Procuradoria-Geral da República informou que "a investigação foi aberta após uma denúncia apresentada por integrantes do Bloco de Esquerda", sem dar mais detalhes.

O Ministério das Relações Exteriores de Portugal não comentou o caso, segundo a Reuters.

Em abril, o Bloco de Esquerda pediu ao Ministério Público que investigasse o uso da Base das Lajes pelos Estados Unidos , sob o argumento de que haveria uma "grave violação do direito internacional".

O ministro das Relações Exteriores, Paulo Rangel, afirmou, por outro lado, que Portugal não estava envolvido no conflito e que o uso da Base das Lajes respeitava o direito internacional. Segundo ele, a autorização só foi concedida após os Estados Unidos garantirem que qualquer operação seria defensiva, necessária e proporcional, além de limitada a alvos militares.

Em Portugal, o Ministério Público é obrigado a investigar suspeitas de irregularidades quando há fundamentos suficientes para isso, devido ao chamado princípio da legalidade. Em alguns países, promotores têm maior liberdade para decidir se um caso deve ou não prosseguir.

A Base das Lajes fica no arquipélago português dos Açores, no Oceano Atlântico, e funciona como um ponto estratégico para o trânsito das forças americanas. Seu uso pelos Estados Unidos está previsto em um acordo bilateral de defesa firmado em 1951.

A base também abriga a 65ª Ala de Base Aérea da Força Aérea dos EUA, que dá apoio a operações americanas, da Otan e de países aliados.

articles.summary: O pesquisador Leonardo Calderon, da Fiocruz e Unir, faleceu aos 50 anos em Porto Velho após sofrer um mal súbito em sua residência no último sábado.
articles.body:
Leonardo calderon — Foto: Arquivo pessoal de Leonardo Calderon

Morreu na manhã deste sábado (3), aos 50 anos, o pesquisador em saúde pública da Fundação Oswaldo Cruz (Fiocruz Rondônia) e professor de medicina da Universidade Federal de Rondônia (Unir), Leonardo Calderon. Ele faleceu na própria casa, vítima de causas naturais decorrentes de um mal súbito.

Cientista renomado, Calderon contribuiu com importantes pesquisas no estado e publicou artigos em diversas revistas especializadas ao redor do mundo. Atualmente, ele era membro do Centro de Estudos de Biomoléculas Aplicadas à Saúde (Cebio) da Fiocruz.

O pesquisador deixa a esposa e um filho.

Bacharel e doutor em Ciências Biológicas pela Universidade de Brasília (UnB), Calderon ingressou no Instituto de Pesquisas em Patologias Tropicais (Ipepatro) em 2008. Ele fez parte de toda a transição do instituto para a criação da Fiocruz Rondônia, onde atuava como pesquisador em saúde pública desde 2012.

Além da pesquisa de bancada, o cientista assumiu importantes posições de liderança acadêmica ao longo da carreira:

Foi vice-diretor de pesquisa da Fiocruz Rondônia entre 2012 e 2014;

Atuou como pró-reitor de pós-graduação e pesquisa da Unir entre 2017 e 2018.

Defensor do acesso à informação, Calderon também se empenhava na divulgação científica para o público em geral e contribuía como colunista da rádio CBN Amazônia, em Porto Velho.

articles.title: Trump divulga celular de senador e pede horário de verão permanente | G1
articles.standfirst: Parlamentar Tom Cotton é contra a mudança e diz que medida deixaria manhãs de inverno mais escuras; projeto já passou pela Câmara, mas enfrenta resistência no Senado.
articles.summary: Parlamentar Tom Cotton é contra a mudança e diz que medida deixaria manhãs de inverno mais escuras; projeto já passou pela Câmara, mas enfrenta resistência no Senado.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , pressionou neste sábado (3) o senador Tom Cotton, do Arkansas, a apoiar um projeto de lei que tornaria permanente o horário de verão no país . O republicano publicou nas redes sociais o que parecia ser o número de celular pessoal do congresssita, e pediu que moradores do estado ligassem para pressioná-lo.

Cotton, que preside o Comitê de Inteligência do Senado e integra a liderança republicana, é contrário à mudança. O projeto já foi aprovado pela Câmara dos Representantes ( equivalente à Câmara dos Deputados), mas enfrenta resistência no Senado.

Trump afirmou que Cotton estaria impedindo a aprovação da proposta e pediu que moradores do Arkansas cobrassem o senador.

"Então, todos no Arkansas, um estado que amo e onde venci três vezes, a última por 34 pontos, digam a Tom para FAZER ISSO!", escreveu Trump.

O número divulgado por Trump tinha código de área do Arkansas. A Associated Press ligou para o telefone, mas ninguém atendeu. A caixa postal também estava cheia.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com a imprensa ao sair da Casa Branca, no gramado sul, em Washington, DC, EUA, em 26 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Annabelle Gordon/Reuters

O texto, conhecido como Sunshine Protection Act, prevê que o horário de verão deixe de ser encerrado no outono e passe a vigorar durante todo o ano.

Atualmente, na maior parte dos Estados Unidos, os relógios são adiantados em uma hora na primavera e atrasados novamente no outono.

Os defensores da mudança, entre eles a Casa Branca, dizem que a medida permitiria mais horas de luz no fim do dia, período em que os americanos costumam estar mais ativos.

Os críticos afirmam que a mudança teria o efeito contrário nas manhãs de inverno. O nascer do sol ocorreria mais tarde, deixando crianças à espera dos ônibus escolares e trabalhadores a caminho do trabalho no escuro.

O projeto foi aprovado pela Câmara em julho, mas enfrenta dificuldades no Senado. Alguns republicanos são contrários à proposta.

Os estados poderiam optar por não adotar o horário de verão permanente caso suas legislaturas aprovassem essa decisão antes da entrada da lei em vigor.

Cotton reafirmou sua oposição ao projeto em uma publicação nas redes sociais.

"Ninguém gosta de mudar o relógio, eu inclusive, mas o Congresso já aprovou o horário de verão permanente várias vezes e o revogou todas as vezes depois que os americanos experimentaram amanheceres absurdamente tardios no inverno", escreveu.

"Os habitantes do Arkansas não querem que seus filhos vão para a escola na escuridão total, e eu sempre colocarei o Arkansas em primeiro lugar", afirmou.

Cotton não é o único republicano contrário à proposta.

Trump já divulgou telefone de outro senador

Esta não é a primeira vez que Trump divulga informações pessoais de um senador que o criticou.

Durante a disputa pela indicação republicana à Presidência em 2016, o então senador Lindsey Graham, da Carolina do Sul, afirmou que Trump era "inapto para o cargo" depois que o então candidato criticou o serviço militar do senador John McCain, do Arizona.

Trump respondeu divulgando o número pessoal de Graham. O episódio levou o senador a gravar um vídeo que viralizou, no qual ele destruiu vários celulares antigos.

Graham se tornou posteriormente um aliado próximo de Trump.

Uma pesquisa realizada em 2025 pelo Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research mostrou que, entre os americanos que preferem uma mudança no sistema, a opção por manter a luz do dia por mais tempo no período da noite é a mais comum.

Segundo o levantamento, apenas 12% dos adultos americanos são favoráveis ao sistema atual, que exige a mudança dos relógios duas vezes por ano na maior parte do país. Outros 47% são contrários e 40% não têm posição.

O Congresso debate os possíveis benefícios e custos do horário de verão há décadas. A medida foi adotada nos Estados Unidos como uma estratégia de guerra em 1942.

Em 2022, o Senado aprovou um projeto para tornar o horário de verão permanente, mas a proposta não avançou na Câmara.

articles.title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
articles.summary: Pike's lawyers said the failure "goes far beyond any one person". Pike is in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections.
articles.body:
The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday.

Governor Bill Lee announced the change on Saturday, sharing the news in a joint statement with Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada.

Strada said that his stepping down is "in the best interests" of the state, and called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".

Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, survived two injections and is now in critical condition at a Tennessee hospital as her lawyers seek to commute her sentence.

"Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment," Lee said.

Lee has ordered an independent review into Pike's attempted execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.

Attorney's for Pike called the resignation "justified" but said "it does nothing to help Christa now".

"What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," Pike's legal team wrote in a statement. "We hope the Governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee's entire death penalty system."

Pike is being treated at a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, where doctors are attempting to clear the drugs used during the execution from her body, according to legal filings.

She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance. While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.

As of Thursday night, she was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator.

The state's Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her failed execution.

Pike's attorneys previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.

The attempted execution went ahead after multiple failed, last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers.

The US Supreme Court rejected two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.

Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.

She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

articles.title: Ramsey mural aims to 'elevate' famous Manx poet
articles.summary: Situated in Parliament Street, the mural celebrates Josephine Kermode, known by her name the Cushag.
articles.body:
A new mural in the north of the Isle of Man aims to "celebrate and elevate" a famous Manx poet, the artist behind the project has said.

Located in Parliament Street, Ramsey, the five-metre (16ft) high mural depicts Josephine Kermode, who published her poems, plays and stories under the name Cushag 100 years ago.

Born in 1852, just two doors down from where the mural has been created, Kermode's poems and plays continue to be performed on the island.

Illustrator Jo Davies said: "It was important for me to make an artwork that wasn't just a picture to decorate a wall but to celebrate, and literally elevate a Ramsey-born woman who made an important contribution to Manx culture."

The work incorporates one of Kermode's best-known poems, which celebrates the Manx national flower's beauty and place in Manx folklore.

"If, like me, people passing don't understand the Manx words I hope that they will appreciate them as things of beauty and over time begin to recognise and connect to them as part of their lives," Ramsey-based Davies said.

Having published her first poetry book in 1907, Kermode created a steady stream of poems and plays throughout her lifetime.

James Franklin, from Culture Vannin said: "Although it is certainly a beautiful image which enhances the experience of Parliament Street, this mural is so much more.

"In confidently placing Cushag, her poetry and the Manx language at the centre of it all, this piece by Jo Davies empowers us to connect to one of the island's great poets whilst tying us to the treasure of its language and the sense of place."

The mural is accompanied by a QR code where those passing by can listen to the poem in both English and Manx.

It is part of a year-long celebration of the Manx language, which aims to create a lasting boost to the island's native tongue.

articles.title: Meet Auntie Juan: 60-year-old Chinese woman who started gaming to understand her son’s addiction, but is now a gaming star
articles.summary: For years, Zhong Juanjuan saw video games as something that was taking her son away from his studies.
articles.body: For years, Zhong Juanjuan saw video games as something that was taking her son away from his studies.Today, the 60-year-old Chinese woman spends hours playing them herself, with thousands of people tuning in to watch.Known online as “Auntie Juan”, Zhong has turned an unusual family story into an unexpected second career. She started playing computer games in 2020, when she was in her 50s. Six years later, she has more than 5 lakh followers and typically attracts around 10,000 viewers to each of her daily livestreams, according to the South China Morning Post.But the surprising part isn't just her age. It’s how she got here.She once dragged her son out of gaming cafesZhong grew up in Meizhou in Guangdong province and completed only primary school. Over the years, she worked a number of jobs, including selling clothes, working in sales and looking after children. She retired around a decade ago.Gaming, however, had already been part of her family story long before she picked up a mouse.Around two decades ago, her younger son, known online as Suode, became heavily involved in gaming while he was still in secondary school. His grades suffered, and Zhong would go looking for him at internet cafes.Sometimes, she would simply pull him out and take him home.So when the same son was spending long hours gaming again years later, Zhong's first reaction could easily have been to repeat the old argument.Instead, she decided to find out what he was so interested in.It started during the pandemicIn 2020, when the Covid-19 pandemic kept families indoors, Zhong watched Suode spend hours playing games at home after leaving his job.She was curious.Rather than simply telling him to stop, she asked him to teach her.Suode was surprised, but he agreed.The first lessons weren't exactly smooth. Zhong struggled to control her character, often walking straight into walls, turning the wrong way and even having trouble getting up virtual stairs. Her eyesight was also declining, while her reactions were naturally slower than those of younger players.But she kept going.And that turned out to be the beginning of something neither mother nor son expected.From struggling beginner to serious gamerZhong didn't just learn to play casually. She started spending hours practising and gradually became good at shooting games, particularly Counter-Strike.Her son, who had spent years playing games himself, taught her things such as positioning, aiming and when to attack or defend. The two also started discussing gaming tactics, sometimes disagreeing over what move to make.The roles inside the family were slowly changing.The mother who once complained about her son's gaming was now asking him about weapons, strategies and gameplay.At one point, Zhong became so engrossed in the game that she lost track of time. According to Economic Observer, she would sometimes play until late at night, prompting Suode to eventually set the home Wi-Fi to switch off automatically so she would stop playing and get some sleep.Her gaming hours soon began to add up.By early 2026, reports put her Counter-Strike playing time at more than 8,000 hours. She also plays other games, but shooting games remain her main focus.Her son told her to start livestreamingAfter seeing how much time his mother was spending on games, Suode suggested that she try livestreaming.Zhong took the idea seriously.She began streaming in 2022 and slowly built an audience. Her basic setup, her age and, most of all, her gaming skills made her stand out from the crowd.There was something almost surreal about watching a woman who had only recently learned to use a gaming mouse sit in front of a computer and play a fast-paced shooting game with the confidence of someone who had been doing it for years.Her streams also became known for her casual use of gaming slang.And then came the doubts.Some viewers thought she was not really playingAs Zhong's skills became more noticeable, some viewers refused to believe that a woman approaching 60 could actually play at that level.People online accused her of using someone else to control the game or suggested that the videos were somehow fake.Her son decided to address the accusations in a very simple way.He installed multiple cameras so viewers could see Zhong, her hands and the screen from different angles while she played. That allowed people watching the livestream to see that she was actually controlling the game herself.There were even more unusual rumours about her past. Some online users speculated that she must have been a highly skilled machine operator or an experienced industrial worker because of the precision of her shooting.Zhong reportedly laughed at the idea.She had no idea what the job they were talking about even meant.The Counter-Strike match that changed everythingZhong's biggest breakthrough came in 2024.In December that year, when she was 58, she was invited to take part in a Counter-Strike exhibition match. One of the players on the other side was Danil “donk” Kryshkovets, the teenage Russian esports star who had become one of the biggest names in competitive Counter-Strike.And Zhong managed to eliminate him with a single precise shot.The moment did not immediately turn her into a global internet sensation. According to Economic Observer, the clip received much more attention months later when first-person footage was released and gamers began analysing the play frame by frame.That was when many younger gamers began paying attention to the woman they had come to know as Auntie Juan.Reports in 2026 also said she later took part in another friendly exhibition match involving professional players, where she managed to eliminate both donk and fellow Team Spirit player Dmitriy “sh1ro” Sokolov in the game. The moment spread widely among gaming communities.It was, of course, one round in an exhibition match and not evidence that she had suddenly become a professional esports player. But for a woman who had picked up gaming only a few years earlier, it was enough to make her a viral name.“Should I only be relegated to household chores?”Her popularity has also brought an entirely different conversation.Some people have questioned why a woman her age spends so much time gaming. The assumption, as Zhong has pointed out, is that women of her generation should stick to more traditional roles.She has pushed back against that idea.“As a mother, should I only be relegated to household chores?” she asked, according to India Today. She has also said that gaming keeps her mind active and helps with hand-eye coordination. Her message is simple: starting something new doesn't have to come with an age limit.And perhaps the biggest irony is that the woman who once tried to stop her son from playing games is now the one who needs to be told when to switch them off.Suode, who once had his gaming interrupted by his mother, is now her full-time agent. He helps with her videos, livestreaming and other work around her online career. He also makes sure she doesn't stay up gaming all night.From selling clothes to becoming a gaming starZhong's story isn't only about gaming.Before becoming Auntie Juan, she had spent much of her life working to support her family. Economic Observer reported that she had sold clothes on the streets, worked as a salesperson and later worked as a childcare provider. She had no formal higher education and had lived most of her life in Meizhou.Gaming changed that.By 2025, her income from gaming was reportedly around ten times what she had earned before she became a streamer, and she had become the main earner in her family. Her son, who once had a job as a software engineer, now works behind the scenes managing her online career.Her family has even created a dedicated gaming room for her, complete with computers and equipment.Yet Zhong apparently doesn't make a big deal about her online fame in everyday life.She has reportedly been hesitant to tell people in her neighbourhood that she is a gaming streamer because she worries they might think she is boasting. On one occasion, she was surprised when someone from her village told her they had seen her on Douyin.Then there are moments that remind her just how far things have gone.Recently, a man recognised her at a wet market and told her that he had watched her gaming online.For Zhong, the journey began with a simple question: why did her son enjoy games so much?She thought she was entering his world to understand him better.Instead, she found a world of her own.You use AI every day. articles.title: Man shot dead in East Acton as people gather for memorial service
articles.summary: The 40-year-old died at the scene in west London from a gunshot wound, the Met Police said.
articles.body:
A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people – including children – gathered for a memorial service in west London.

The Met Police said it was called to the scene at 19:47 GMT on Friday after multiple shots had been heard by members of the public at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton.

Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service but the man was pronounced dead at the scene, despite the efforts of medics.

No arrests have been made and a police cordon remains in place in Braybrook Street. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.

The victim's family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.

A post-mortem examination is scheduled to establish the cause of death, but the victim is believed to have sustained a gunshot wound, the force said.

Det Ch Insp Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said: "Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence.

"We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated.

"We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward."

He has asked anyone who was around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 18:00 and 20:00, to "please think carefully about what you saw".

He added: "Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously, or vehicles being driven at speed?

"We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media.

"However insignificant it may seem, the smallest piece of information could prove crucial in helping us establish what happened and identify those responsible."

articles.title: A 2,000-year-old water channel still flows beneath Smyrna after surviving earthquakes and now irrigates parks in Izmir
articles.summary: A channel built about 2,000 years ago still carries water beneath the ancient city of Smyrna in present-day Izmir, Türkiye.
articles.body: A channel built about 2,000 years ago still carries water beneath the ancient city of Smyrna in present-day Izmir, Türkiye. The channel was built beneath streets and houses and still carries water today. The main channel stretches 150 metres and is large enough for a person to walk through comfortably. Water still flows from a spring into the channel, even during summer. Archaeologists are continuing excavations at Smyrna to uncover more of the ancient city and preserve its remains. According to Türkiye Today, Smyrna has been on UNESCO’s World Heritage Tentative List since 2020 as part of the ‘Historical Port City of Izmir’ listing.How did Smyrna’s ancient water channel carry water through the cityThe main water channel reaching the Smyrna Agora is 150 metres long, 2.16 metres high and 90 centimetres wide. Its size allows a person to walk inside it comfortably. The channel was built under streets and houses around 2,000 years ago. Water still travels through the system from a spring, flowing at a height of 1.5 metres from the spring to the channel.The network was part of Smyrna’s underground water system, which connected natural springs to fountains and bathhouses. One channel running through the agora divided into two branches. One branch supplied the Roman bath, while the other led to the Gymnasium.How is the ancient water channel being used todayThe water flowing through the ancient channel is still being used, although it is not suitable for drinking. Tests found nitrate levels were 1.5 times the accepted limits, while arsenic levels were twice the accepted limits. Professor Akin Ersoy said the water is instead used to irrigate the grass in the Smyrna Agora and green spaces in the city.The ancient baths no longer function, but the water continues to flow throughout the year, including summer. The excavation team now uses the water to irrigate nearby green spaces instead of letting it flow away unused. Ersoy also noted that the sound of running water creates a relaxing atmosphere for visitors.Smyrna’s Roman infrastructure included water channels, fountains, and public buildingsSmyrna’s water system formed part of a larger city infrastructure that expanded during the early Roman Empire under Augustus. The ancient city stood between Kemeralti and Kadifekale, while springs were identified along the slopes of Kadifekale. The agora was surrounded by porticos with columned facades, fountains and water channels.Smyrna also had one of the largest agoras from antiquity and one of the grandest theatres in the Mediterranean region. Excavations have uncovered thousands of artefacts dating from the Hellenistic period to the late Ottoman era. Roman-era household objects include bowls, plates, basins, strainers, lamps, jugs, weaving weights and lids dating from the first to fourth centuries A.D.Smyrna’s ancient city survived earthquakes and centuries of changeThe ancient city of Smyrna has a history stretching back to the late fourth century B.C., following the reign of Alexander the Great. According to the ancient geographer Pausanias, Alexander founded the city after a dream in which the goddess Nemesis told him to build it on Pagos Hill (modern-day Kadifekale). His generals, Antigonos and Lysimachos, later oversaw its relocation and construction. The agora served as a commercial, political, and judicial hub until an earthquake destroyed it in 178 A.D.Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius ordered its reconstruction, and most surviving ruins belong to this later phase. Excavations began in 1933 and were revived in 2007 under Associate Professor Akin Ersoy and his team. Since 2020, the ancient city has been officially included on UNESCO’s World Heritage Tentative List under the name ‘Historical Port City of Izmir’.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Rare humpback whale spotted on Pembrokeshire coast
articles.summary: Wildlife cameraman Dan Abbot is caught off guard by a humpback whale, a rare sight in Welsh waters.
articles.body:
A wildlife cinematographer and shark guide has spoken about the unexpected surprise and joy of seeing a humpback whale in the Celtic Deep just off the Welsh coast.

Dan Abbot, known as Sharkman Dan on his social media, shared a recording of the exciting moment just off the Pembrokeshire coast.

He has seen the large marine mammals before, on planned trips where humpback whale sightings are not as unusual, but this experience was "a complete surprise".

Lloyd Nelmes from Sea Trust said the sighting was "unusual for someone who works in the field... who probably has their eyes on the water every day", adding, "for a normal person, it's insanely rare".

Abbot guides blue shark snorkelling trips off of Pembrokeshire and was on a scheduled snorkelling trip in the Celtic Sea on 25 September when he discovered the rare find.

The group had just left the snorkelling site after seeing multiple sharks and were 25-30 miles offshore.

Abbot recalled seeing lots of feeding going on among bluefin tuna, dolphins and gannets which he said was not unusual in the waters there at this time of year.

When a guest on board "saw a whale blow in the distance", Abbot inititally suspected it was a minke or fin whale, the two most common whales in Welsh waters.

"I said if it's a big blow, then it's probably a fin whale," he said.

"So we then watched it blowing, quite far out, and slowly moved towards the area where there was lots of feeding going on because sometimes you can see whales lunge feeding."

"As we got a bit closer and parked the boat a bit to let things develop around us, I noticed that when it came up for a blow, it actually had white pectoral fin, which fin whales don't have," Abbot said.

"And then the other thing they don't do is they don't lift their tails out of the water, which humpbacks do. You could see barnacles around the front of the head, which fin whales don't have.

"I actually went quiet for a moment. At that point, it was pretty clear it was a humpback whale."

He continued: "I don't really get that excited, which sounds strange. I'm usually one of the quietest ones on the boat, but I think it was just because it was such a surprise to see that species.

"I'm a wildlife cameraman but when something happens like that unexpectedly and catches you off guard, there's something about it that kind of makes it even more special."

Guests on the boat were already in high spirits after the four-hour snorkelling trip, but Abbot said 'then to see a humpback whale was just an incredible way to finish the day".

Lloyd Nelmes, an aquarium manger and marine project officer with Sea Trust Wales, spotted a humpback whale in Pembrokeshire in 2024.

Nelmes said: "The whale jumped out right in front of us. It was incredible, and it's still probably my top wildlife moment of my life."

He explained that humpback whale sightings were rare but not unheard of in Welsh waters, with sightings happening once every two or three years.

Nelmes said the way to spot a humpback whale was by the overall shape, white pectoral fins, and knobbly skin also known as barnacles, as well as the whales' behaviour.

"We've seen humpbacks here on the rare occasion... but it seems to be becoming more common, which is awesome," he said.

"It's quite likely just an indication of how much food is about at the moment."

He said he had been on an "incredible" trip out to the Celtic Deep the day before Abbot's discovery and had seen six fin whales, tuna balling up and 1,000-plus dolphins, adding it was not too surprising that a humpack was "out there also making the most of the food".

articles.title: Mother's £1 million home went to the daughter who cared for her; three brothers challenged the will years later
articles.summary: In her latter years Anna Rea changed her will and left her main asset, a South London home, to her daughter Rita who had taken care of her for years.
articles.body: In her latter years Anna Rea changed her will and left her main asset, a South London home, to her daughter Rita who had taken care of her for years. The decision overturned a previous settlement that had split her estate evenly among her four children. After Anna died in 2016, her three sons challenged the new will, alleging that Rita had unduly influenced their mother. There was a long legal battle, including two trials and several appeals. The dispute eventually reached the Court of Appeal, which upheld the 2015 will in 2024.Mother’s £1 million home at the centre of dispute between her childrenAnna had lived at 5 Brenda Road in Tooting Bec, London, since 1964, and the house became the central asset in the family dispute. According to the ProMediate account of Rea v Rea, Anna had four children including 3 sons named Remo, Nino and David, and one daughter Rita. Her 1986 will had divided her estate equally between the four.By 2015, the family situation had changed considerably. Anna had suffered a heart attack in 2009 and needed increasing support. Rita moved back into the family home and became her principal carer. The 2023 High Court judgment recorded that Rita lived with her mother from 2009 and that the extent of the care she provided was not disputed, although the brothers and Rita disagreed about their own involvement in caring for Anna.The value of the property was substantial. The original court evidence described the house as worth about £750,000 at the time of the 2015 will, while later reports put the value at close to £1 million. The home was effectively the main asset of Anna's estate.What changed in Anna Rea's final willOn 7 December 2015, Anna signed a new will prepared by solicitor Savita Sukul. It gave the house to Rita, while the remainder of the estate was still divided equally between the four children. The will also recorded Anna's reasons for treating her daughter differently, pointing to Rita's years of care and her view that her sons had not provided the assistance she expected.The change was significant because the earlier will had remained in place for nearly 30 years. The brothers later argued that the new arrangement was not the result of their mother's independent decision.This was not just a legal case of Anna changing her mind or not. Her sons challenged the will on a number of grounds including lack of testamentary capacity, lack of knowledge and approval, undue influence and fraudulent calumny. The central issue eventually became whether Rita had coerced her mother into making the change.Why did the three brothers challenge the willThe brothers questioned the circumstances surrounding the new will and argued that their mother's age, frailty and dependence on Rita made her vulnerable. They also pointed to Rita's involvement in arranging the solicitor's appointment and the fact that the new will was not disclosed to them before Anna died.The High Court's 2023 retrial accepted several of those concerns. Judge Hodge KC found that Anna had the mental capacity to make a will and understood what the document contained, but concluded that Rita had exercised undue influence over her. The judge therefore declared the 2015 will invalid and restored the position under the 1986 will.That ruling was not the final word, however. Rita appealed, taking the dispute back to the Court of Appeal.Decision taken by Court of AppealIn February 2024, the Court of Appeal unanimously allowed Rita's appeal and restored the 2015 will. The judges concluded that the evidence did not establish the level of coercion required to prove undue influence in a will.FootAnstey reported that the court considered there was a rational explanation for Anna's decision. Rita had lived with her and cared for her for years, while Anna believed her sons had not provided the same level of care. The court also considered the evidence from the solicitor and GP who had been involved in preparing and witnessing the will.Paul Robinson's legal analysis reported that the case reaffirmed an important distinction regarding inheritance disputes. Influence, persuasion, family disagreement or dependency do not automatically amount to undue influence. The evidence must show that the person's free choice was overcome by coercion.How did professional checks affect the final rulingThe preparation of Anna's will became particularly important during the appeals. The solicitor had taken instructions directly from Anna and was satisfied that she understood what she wanted. She also arranged for Anna's GP, Dr Sajid Abdul Qaiyum, to assess her capacity because of her age and the substantial change from the earlier will.The GP found Anna capable and did not identify evidence that she was being coerced. Rita was also absent when the final will was executed. These details later carried considerable weight when the Court of Appeal reconsidered the High Court's findings.How long did the family inheritance fight lastAnna died on 26 July 2016, aged 85. The legal proceedings began the following year and continued through an original trial, appeals, a retrial and another appeal. The final Court of Appeal decision came in February 2024, bringing almost seven years of litigation to an end.The route to that decision was particularly complicated. The first trial upheld the 2015 will. A subsequent appeal resulted in an order for a new trial because the brothers had been unfairly restricted in cross-examining Rita. At the 2023 retrial, the brothers succeeded, only for that decision to be overturned by the Court of Appeal the following year.The Court of Appeal had earlier urged the family to consider mediation when it ordered the retrial, warning about the emotional and financial consequences of continuing the dispute. The case nevertheless continued through another trial and appeal.The final ruling meant that Anna's 2015 will remain valid. Rita retained the gift of the Tooting Bec family home, while the remainder of Anna's estate was to be divided between all four children according to the terms of that will.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tennessee prisons official resigns after Christa Pike’s failed US execution
articles.summary: The state’s governor said Frank Strada would step down as an independent review examines what went wrong.
articles.body:
The official in charge of the prison system in the US state of Tennessee has resigned just days after overseeing the botched execution of Christa Pike.

The state’s governor, Bill Lee, announced on Saturday that Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada would step down from his role later this month, a decision Lee described as necessary after the stunning failure.

“Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment”, Lee said in a statement. “I have accepted his decision to step down and am grateful for his commitment to ensuring a smooth leadership transition”.

A replacement for Strada was not announced.

Strada, who started his role in Tennessee three years ago, previously served as a top official in Arizona’s corrections department where multiple executions on his watch faced complications. He said he was resigning “in the best interest of Tennesseans” as an independent review examines what went wrong.

“I believe this review is entirely appropriate and necessary, and I look forward to doing everything I can to help determine exactly what occurred,” Strada said in a statement that defended his department’s handling of Pike’s execution.

Pike was transported from prison to hospital on Wednesday after surviving two injections of the drug pentobarbital, which Tennessee uses to execute prisoners.

Strada’s resignation was “justified”, Pike’s lawyers said in a statement. “But it does nothing to help Christa now.”

“What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person,” they wrote. “We hope the Governor’s call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee’s entire death penalty system.”

In a court filing on Friday, Pike’s lawyers said she had been placed on a ventilator and intubated as medical staff worked to clear the drug from her system. They argued problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream.

“Apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realise that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms Pike’s body,” they wrote in the filing.

Pike was 18 years old when she was sentenced to death for the torture and murder of another young woman in 1995, becoming one of the youngest women to be sent to death row.

Lee has suspended all executions for the remainder of the year while the state investigates.

articles.title: Sir Kevin Sinfield completes epic challenge ahead of Grand Final
articles.summary: Sir Kevin Sinfield crosses the finish line at Old Trafford after seven ultramarathons in seven days.
articles.body:
Sir Kevin Sinfield has completed his latest endurance challenge raising money for motor neurone disease (MND) causes in memory of his friend and teammate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024.

Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final.

The fundraiser and his team have raised more than £13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020.

Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us."

Sinfield began his final ultramarathon challenge in Hull on September 27 and visited all 12 Super League clubs along the way.

The 7 in 7: The Grand Finale week ended at Old Trafford earlier where he brought out the trophy ahead of the game between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity.

Along the way he was surprised by royals , including The Prince and Princess of Wales and the Princess Royal, as well as famous names from the sporting world such as former England football manager Sir Gareth Southgate and Leeds boxer Josh Warrington.

Each day was split into 7km, hour-long blocks with an additional extra mile for members of the MND community to join.

Funds raised by the challenge will go towards the work of the MND Association, Leeds Hospitals Charity, My Name5 Doddie Foundation, Darby Rimmer Foundation, MND Scotland and the Irish MND Association.

Sinfield, 45, who played his entire professional career with Leeds Rhinos, is one of the most successful players in Super League history.

He and Burrow met at the Leeds Rhinos academy aged 14 and 12. They went on to win seven titles together with Leeds Rhinos.

Burrow's wife, Lindsey Burrow, told BBC Radio 4's PM that her late husband "would have been incredibly proud" of his friend.

"It's bittersweet that Rob's not here today to see Kevin finish his final challenge but Rob will be with us in spirit and it's just testimony to Kevin that he's so humbled to do this not just for Rob but for the whole MND community," Lindsey said.

"It's just incredible. I am in complete awe of the efforts of Kevin and his team over the last seven days, and not just over the last seven days but over the last seven years," she added.

Sinfield's son, Jack Sinfield, lined up in the Wakefield side seeking to clinch their first top-flight title since 1968.

articles.title: Algeria sent fighter jets to Niger to thwart ‘coup attempt’, president says
articles.summary: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune says Algiers deployed warplanes to Niamey in late August following an attack by mutineers.
articles.body:
Algeria’s President Abdelmadjid Tebboune has said that his country sent fighter jets to Niger in late August to help thwart a “ coup attempt ” that shook the capital, Niamey.

The confirmation came in excerpts from Tebboune’s interview with local media outlets that was broadcast on Saturday ahead of its full release.

Tebboune said that the warplanes were sent because some parties had “gone too far”.

He added that Niger’s Prime Minister, Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, had been visiting Algeria and returned home at night just before the mutiny.

“For obvious reasons, this is a provocation against us … and I too will send planes and we’ll meet head-on,” Tebboune said.

He did not specify who he meant when he said some had gone too far, or whether he was referring to internal or external actors.

Sustained gunfire and explosions were heard in Niamey overnight on August 28 into August 29.

A military base at Diori Hamani International Airport was first targeted by renegade soldiers, followed by attacks on the state broadcaster and presidential palace.

Niger’s Minister of Defence, General Salifou Modi, announced at the time that a group of military personnel attempted to detain a number of their colleagues at Air Base 101, and opened fire on strategic locations in the capital.

Security forces had intervened and managed to contain the situation, gradually regaining control over the targeted locations, he added.

On August 30 , the Algerian Ministry of Defence said it had sent four fighter jets to Niger following unrest. It said two patrols of four Sukhoi Su-30 aircraft had landed at Niamey airport, accompanied by an air-to-air refuelling plane.

The warplanes were deployed at the request of Nigerien authorities on “a mission to support the Nigerien army in confronting an attempt to destabilise the brotherly state of Niger,” the ministry added then.

Niger’s military government last month accused France of orchestrating the failed mutiny, but France denied any involvement in the events in its former colony.

Algeria and Niger share close security and military ties, as well as a long land border, with Algeria viewing the stability of the Sahel region as an essential component of its national security.

Niger’s Prime Minister Zeine met President Tebboune when he visited Algeria on August 26–27 as the head of a high-level ministerial delegation aimed at enhancing cooperation between the two countries.

articles.title: At 6, Los Angeles boy Dylan Siegel wrote Chocolate Bar to help his best friend Jonah, who had a rare liver disorder; two years later, the book had raised $1 million for research into the disease
articles.summary: At the age of 6, Los Angeles boy Dylan Siegel decided he wanted to help his best friend, Jonah Pournazarian, who had a rare genetic disorder affecting his
articles.body: At the age of 6, Los Angeles boy Dylan Siegel decided he wanted to help his best friend, Jonah Pournazarian, who had a rare genetic disorder affecting his liver. When his mother suggested that he could raise money through a lemonade stand, Dylan had another idea. He wanted to write a book.The result was a 14-page illustrated booklet called Chocolate Bar. According to Jewish Journal, Dylan used the phrase “Chocolate Bar” to describe things he thought were great, including trips to Disneyland, the swimming pool, the aquarium and the bowling alley. He ended the book with a line about helping his friends.Dylan did not stop with writing the book. He worked with his parents to produce copies and started selling them to raise money for research into glycogen storage disease type 1B, the disorder affecting Jonah. The book was sold for $20, while chocolate bars carrying the same design were also sold as part of the fundraising effort.The project began on a small scale in late 2012. Dylan and Jonah sold the books and chocolate bars at their school’s Mitzvah Day, where the effort raised about $7,000 for GSD research. As more people heard about the project through book fairs and television reports, the number of copies sold grew. By December 2014, Chocolate Bar had raised $1 million for research into the disease.Jonah's rare liver disorderJonah was one of a very small number of children living with glycogen storage disease type 1B. The Jewish Journal reported in January 2013 that fewer than 100 cases of type 1B had been identified in the United States at that time.Glycogen storage disease affects the way the body handles glycogen, the stored form of glucose. Normally, the body breaks down glycogen and converts it into energy. This process depends on enzymes. In people with GSD, problems with these enzymes can slow down or stop the process.There are 14 known categories of GSD. Type 1B is one of seven types that primarily affect the liver. In Jonah’s case, glucose was stored in his liver and could not properly get out, according to his doctor.The condition had a major effect on Jonah from the time he was born. He weighed 4 pounds at birth and was frequently ill. He had very low or barely detectable sugar and white blood cell counts, suffered from severe diarrhoea and sometimes woke up covered in sweat.His family later sought treatment from Dr David A. Weinstein, a paediatric endocrinologist at the University of Florida, Gainesville, who was working on GSD treatment and research. Medical consultations required Jonah and his family to travel to Florida.Treatment meant living by the clockBy the time the Jewish Journal wrote about Jonah in 2013, his treatment required regular doses of cornstarch. The treatment had to be given through a surgically implanted feeding tube every three to four hours, including during the night.Jonah’s mother, Lora Pournazarian, described the routine saying, “We live by the clock.” She and her husband, Rabin Pournazarian, kept two alarm clocks in their bedroom, both set for 3am, so they could wake up and give Jonah his early-morning dose.Missing a feeding could have serious consequences. The Jewish Journal reported that the consequences could range from a short hospital stay to death.Jonah’s parents also tried to ensure that the disease did not stop him from living as normally as possible. During the 2013 report, he was described as playing Monopoly with a friend at home. His mother said the family did not describe him as sick or not normal.At school, his classmates had also adjusted to his medical needs. A medical aide was present with him full time and administered frequent blood tests.Dylan turned friendship into fundraisingDylan’s parents, Debra and David Siegel, were friends of Jonah’s parents and had already been involved in the Jonah Pournazarian Fund to Support Glycogen Storage Disease 1B research. The fund had raised $410,000 by January 2013.Dylan wanted to contribute in his own way. His mother initially suggested a lemonade stand, but Dylan said he wanted to write a book. She thought the idea might pass, but the next day he showed her the finished work.The book began with Dylan describing things he liked as “Chocolate Bar”, meaning something he considered very good. The booklet included his own writing and illustrations. Its final message connected the project to Jonah, “I like to help my friends, that is the biggest Chocolate Bar.”Dylan’s father helped with the production, and the first print run consisted of 200 copies. At the school’s Mitzvah Day in November 2012, Dylan and Jonah sold autographed books for $20 each. They also sold chocolate bars for $5.The first event raised about $7,000. After that, the project continued to grow. A second printing produced 300 copies and a third produced another 500. A Barnes & Noble book fair and television coverage helped bring more attention to the project.By January 2013, about 750 copies had been sold, while the combined proceeds from the books and chocolate bars had reached about $30,000.$1 million reached in 2014The fundraising continued after the early success. The ABC News report published on December 15, 2014, said Chocolate Bar had reached $1 million in book sales that week.The money was directed to the University of Florida laboratory where Weinstein led research into GSD. ABC News reported that every cent from the book went to the lab.The funds supported the hiring of a new geneticist and research that resulted in new gene-therapy treatments. ABC News also reported that the money helped keep the facility operating and on track towards a cure within several years.Dylan said he planned to continue raising money until a cure was found. His original idea at the age of 6 had grown from a small book project into a fundraising effort involving supporters across all 50 US states and more than 60 countries.You use AI every day.
